title: Customer Success KPI Snapshot — Latency, Uptime, Cost/token, Cache Hit
summary: Compact reference for measuring and reporting the four operational KPIs used in customer QBRs: p50/p95 serving latency, service uptime, effective cost-per-token (compute-adjusted), and cache hit metrics. Includes measurement recipes, sample KPI snapshot table, action triggers, and recommended targets by customer tier.
body:
Purpose:
A single-page operational play brief that Customer Success can use to validate renewal conversations during QBRs. Focused on the four signals most correlated with renewal risk for inference customers: latency (end-to-end), uptime (availability/failed requests), cost-per-token (normalized cost signal), and cache hit effectiveness (prefix and kv-cache).

Audience and use:
- Customer Success AEs and Solutions Engineers preparing QBR slides.
- Data analysts producing monthly KPI exports.
- Renewal reviewers deciding whether to propose capacity or optimization interventions.

What this doc contains:
1) Clear, reproducible definitions for each KPI.
2) Short measurement recipes (SQL/ELT pseudo-queries and windowing guidance).
3) A compact, copy-pasteable KPI table (CSV) sample for QBR decks.
4) Action thresholds tied to renewal guidance (investigate, escalate, optimize).

Key definition highlights:
- Latency (p50 / p95 / p99): measured as server-side end-to-end generation time from request accept to final token emitted. Include streaming overhead for streaming customers. Exclude synthetic/health-check traffic and admin tooling calls. Use fixed time-window: last 7 days for operational SLO, last 30 days for trend.
- Uptime (availability): percent of successful requests where HTTP code in [200, 202] and model-level error rate < 0.5%. Report both 30d rolling uptime and business-hours (customer timezone) uptime.
- Cost/token (effective): total billed compute cost attributable to the customer divided by total tokens generated (prompt + generation). When customers have tiered pricing or reserved capacity, use compute-equivalent cost: map committed GPU-hours to on-demand cost to allow cross-customer comparison. Report median and 90th percentile of session-level cost/token to surface heavy outliers.
- Cache hit rate (effective): fraction of token generation requests that reused a cached KV/prefix entry resulting in one of: (1) reduced compute steps (measured via kernel-step delta) or (2) token-level latency reduction > X ms. Provide both raw cache-hit% and effective-cache-save% (compute time saved normalized to total generation time).

Measurement recipes (pseudo-SQL / ELT):
- Latency p95 (7d):
  SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY duration_ms) AS p95_latency
  FROM requests
  WHERE customer_id = :cust AND request_time >= current_date - interval '7 days' AND is_synthetic = false;
- Uptime 30d (business hours):
  SELECT 1.0 - SUM(case when success = false then 1 else 0 end)::float / COUNT(*) AS uptime_30d
  FROM requests
  WHERE customer_id = :cust AND request_time >= current_date - interval '30 days' AND is_business_hour = true;
- Effective cost/token (30d):
  -- compute credits mapped to $ equivalent plus on-demand charges
  SELECT SUM(billed_cost_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(tokens_total),0) AS cost_per_token
  FROM billing_line_items
  WHERE customer_id = :cust AND period >= date_trunc('month', current_date - interval '1 month');
- Cache hit effectiveness (7d):
  SELECT SUM(case when cache_reused then 1 else 0 end)::float / COUNT(*) AS raw_cache_hit_pct,
         SUM(saved_compute_ms) / NULLIF(SUM(duration_ms),1) AS effective_cache_save_pct
  FROM generation_events
  WHERE customer_id = :cust AND event_time >= current_date - interval '7 days';

Smoothing and signal hygiene:
- Present 7d rolling and 30d rolling metrics to avoid noise. For latency show EWMA (alpha=0.3) overlay to reveal persistent shifts versus spikes.
- Annotate any day with infra incidents (SRE incident id) and capacity changes (dedicated capacity on/off) so CS reviewers can separate product regressions from infra events.

Action thresholds and recommended next steps (operationalized):
- Latency:
  - p95 > 1.5x historical baseline for 3 consecutive days -> Investigate model variant routing, check cache warmup, escalate to solutions engineering.
  - p50 stable but p95 rising -> look for tail batching issues or noisy outlier customer requests (very long sequences).
- Uptime:
  - 30d uptime < 99.5% -> open incident review with SRE and map to renewal risk flag.
  - Business-hours uptime < 99% for enterprise customers -> schedule immediate remediation and credit discussion.
- Cost/token:
  - Cost/token > 2x cohort median AND usage growth > 20% month-over-month -> recommend Optimize workshop (quantization, batching, cache policy).
  - Cost/token increasing while latency stable -> possible model drift or token inflation in prompts; run prompt-eval and guidance review.
- Cache hit metrics:
  - Raw cache_hit < 20% for a customer using prefix-caching -> investigate routing/prefix hygiene; check that customer cache keys are stable.
  - Effective_cache_save_pct < 5% despite raw hits > 30% -> cache reuse not producing savings (small payloads or short sequences); consider session-level caching changes.

Notes on reporting cadence and presentation:
- For QBR decks: show headline 30d numbers + variance vs prior quarter and an annotated 7d sparkline for each metric. Use shading for thresholds (green/amber/red).
- Add one row in the QBR slide with the single recommended ask: either (A) apply technical optimization plan, (B) suggest reserved capacity, or (C) negotiate renewal credits. Link to a clear owner and timeframe (30/60/90 days).

Appendix: common pitfalls and false positives:
- Synthetic traffic skew: health checks or synthetic load tests can dramatically reduce apparent latency and increase cache hit; always filter these.
- Multi-region customer usage: compare region-level SLOs before averaging globally; a single-region outage should not always be treated as full-customer degradation if traffic is regionalized.
- Reserved vs on-demand bucket accounting: ensure cost normalization is applied consistently across customers when comparing cost/token.

Contact and escalation path:

- SE escalation: Ethan Park (ethan@redwood.ai)
- SRE incident triage: runbook link in Confluence (linked_artifacts above)

measurement_methods:
Datasource inventory: requests table (per-request timing), generation_events (cache flags, saved_compute_ms), billing_line_items (billed_cost_usd, credits mapping). ETL notes: ensure timezones normalized to customer local TZ, use identical tokenization scheme used by billing. For reserved capacity customers, map committed GpuHours to equivalent $ using internal ratecard (see linked_artifacts).

Quick SQL tips: always use NULLIF to avoid division by zero, use percentile_cont for p95/p99, and compute both absolute and rolling windows to detect fast regressions vs long-term drift.
action_triggers:
Investigate when any of the following occur:
- p95 latency > 1.5x baseline for 72 hours
- 30d uptime < 99.5% or business-hours uptime < 99%
- cost/token > 2x cohort median with >20% MoM usage growth
- raw cache hit < 20% for customers relying on prefix caching
Escalation path:
1) CS owner reproduces metric with raw query and screenshots.
2) Open an SE ticket and attach sample traces (one slow request and one typical request).
3) If infra suspected, file SRE incident and tag customer_id and related routes.
4) Track remediation in renewal tracker (link to tracker in linked_artifacts).
recommended_targets:
Startup / SMB: p95 latency < 700ms, uptime (30d) >= 99.0%, cost/token < $0.0025, raw cache_hit >= 15%
Mid-market: p95 latency < 500ms, uptime >= 99.5%, cost/token < $0.0020, raw_cache_hit >= 25%
Enterprise: p95 latency < 300ms, uptime >= 99.9%, cost/token < $0.0015 (or reserved equivalent), raw_cache_hit >= 35%
Notes: targets are advisory; use customer SLAs and contract terms to set final thresholds.
data_sources: Primary: analytics warehouse (requests, generation_events), billing dataset (billing_line_items), SRE incident tracker. Secondary: SDK logs and customer-provided telemetry. For step-by-step dashboards see Confluence playbook in linked_artifacts.
